key_insight: Dex-One2Many shows that a single human demonstration can seed a dexterous robot policy that goes beyond strict imitation, enabling one demo to generalize to many initial poses, goal poses, and grasps. The key idea is to combine human guidance with exploration so the policy learns useful manipulation skills without needing large robot datasets.
problem_solved: The paper tackles the difficulty of learning dexterous manipulation from only one human video. Pure imitation tends to overfit to the demonstrated motion, while reinforcement learning alone is too hard to explore effectively in high-dimensional dexterous control.
method: Start from a single human demonstration to provide an initial behavioral prior for the robot policy.
Use reinforcement learning to expand beyond the demonstrated trajectory and discover multiple successful manipulation strategies.
Balance motion guidance and exploratory learning so the policy can generalize to unseen object poses, target poses, and grasps.
impact: This matters because it reduces the need for expensive robot teleoperation or large demonstration datasets. For practitioners, it offers a more scalable path to training dexterous manipulation policies that are both sample-efficient and broadly generalizable.
